question.ask: How many referrals are still New?
question.whyItMatters: The coordinator contacts each new referral within one business day.

text.text: Run your clinic from one page. Start with Referrals to contact today, check Visits for today's schedule, and watch Plans of care for visits left and recertification dates. Operational tracking only; clinical notes stay in your clinical system.
A referral that waits three days often books somewhere else. The goal is first contact the same business day and an evaluation within a week.
with the patient's name, the referring practice and provider, the body region and the date received. Set
Check the order: signed by the provider, diagnosis written, and frequency or "evaluate and treat". An unsigned order goes back to the physician's office the same day.
if the patient's plan requires authorization before the evaluation. Many commercial plans and most workers' compensation claims do.
Call within four business hours. Leave one voicemail, then text with your scheduling link or number.
Offer an evaluation slot within five business days with a therapist who sees that body region often.
Collect insurance details on the call: carrier, member ID, subscriber, and whether this is an auto or work injury (those bill differently).
Benefits checked: visit limit per year, copay or coinsurance, deductible remaining
Prior authorization requested if needed, with the evaluation date

cells.text: Call, then a note to the referring office
Mark Lost and tell the referring office in one line

text.text: Closing the loop with the referring office matters. Physicians keep sending patients to clinics that tell them what happened.
Once a month, look at referrals by referring practice. A practice that sends ten patients a quarter deserves a thank-you visit and a short update on the outcomes of the patients they sent.
Insurance details collected after the evaluation, then the first visits are denied.
No prior authorization for the evaluation itself.
Self-referred patients in a state that requires a physician's order after a set number of days; know your state's direct access rule and flag those patients.

pages.title: Plans of care, authorizations and recerts

text.text: The plan of care is what the payer approved and what the therapist is accountable for. Most claim denials in outpatient therapy trace back to an expired plan, an exceeded authorization or a missing progress note.
The therapist writes the plan: diagnosis, goals, frequency and duration.
: diagnosis code, frequency, visits authorized, start date, recertify-by date and the main goal in the patient's own words ("climb a flight of stairs").
Send the plan to the referring physician for signature when the payer requires it, and keep a note of the date it was sent.
: the end of the certified period. A recertification needs a re-evaluation and a new signature before this date.
: the payer's end date. It can be earlier than the plan.
: many payers want one at least every ten visits. The re-evaluation visit type covers it.
column changes to Request more visits when three or fewer remain. Then:
The therapist writes a progress note with measurable change (range of motion, strength, a functional score).
Send the request with the note. Ask the payer for the visit count and the new end date.
when approved. Do not book past the approved count while waiting.
Goals reviewed with the patient and written in the discharge note
Home exercise program printed or sent
Discharge summary sent to the referring provider
Patient's next contact set: a check-in call at four weeks

Ruben's shoulder plan was certified for 60 days. The recert date passed two days ago and his re-evaluation is booked this afternoon. The plan shows Recert due; after the visit the therapist updates the goals, the signed recert goes to the surgeon, and the dates move forward.

text.text: The front desk keeps the schedule full, the copays collected and the notes moving. This routine fits a clinic of two to six therapists.
Voicemails returned; new referrals entered with Contact by today
Today's visits reviewed: anyone near the end of their authorization or past a recert date is flagged to the therapist
Copays due today noted from each patient's
Treatment tables wiped, linens stocked, hot packs at temperature
when the patient arrives. Collect the copay before the session and record it in
When a patient checks out, book the next visit before they leave, matching the plan's frequency. A twice-a-week plan should have the next two visits on the calendar.
after the session. The therapist enters the billed units.
Patients who leave without booking go on the afternoon call list.
Keep a short list of patients who want earlier times.
When a cancellation comes in, call that list before the next patient arrives.
Tuesday and Thursday mornings fill first; offer late afternoons to students and shift workers.
Every completed visit has units entered
Unsigned notes listed and sent to each therapist (notes should be signed within 24 hours)
Copays reconciled against the visits marked completed
Referrals contacted or carried over with a new Contact by date

cells.text: Matches the plan's frequency and duration

text.text: "Same time Thursday, Teodora? Dr. Lindgren has 1 pm open. I'll text a reminder the day before. Your copay today was zero, so you're all set."
Every missed visit is a lost slot and slower progress for the patient. Most no-shows are preventable with reminders and a clear policy explained at the first visit.
Explain the attendance policy at the evaluation and have the patient sign it.
Send a text reminder two days before and the morning of each visit.
Book a standing time (same days, same hour) for the length of the plan. Patients keep routines.
Ask at checkout whether anything next week might get in the way.
When a patient does not arrive
Wait ten minutes, then call. Many are running late and can still be seen for a shorter session.
If no answer, mark the visit
and leave a friendly voicemail with two new times.
Note it on the plan's page with the date.
Tell the treating therapist so they can adjust the plan.
Offer the slot to the waiting list straight away.
Charge the late fee only if your policy says so and the patient signed it. Be consistent; exceptions for illness or emergencies are fine when written down.

cells.text: Review whether the plan still fits; consider discharge with a home program
Offer telehealth visits where the payer covers them

text.text: Report attendance to the case manager or adjuster as their claim requires. Missed visits can affect the patient's claim, so tell the patient that plainly and kindly.
Checklist for the therapist after a second no-show
Call the patient within one business day
Ask what is getting in the way
Agree a new schedule or a discharge with home exercises
Update the plan's page with what was agreed

Kwabena missed two balance sessions. The therapist called; his ride had changed shifts. The clinic moved him to every other Friday afternoon and added a home program. His status went from On hold back to Active.

The front office of an outpatient therapy clinic: referrals coming in, plans of care with their authorized visit counts, the day's schedule, and the notes that still need a signature. Your documentation system keeps the clinical record; this is where the clinic is run.
: every incoming order from a physician, surgeon or self-referral, with the referring provider and whether the payer wants a prior authorization.
: the episode of care. Diagnosis code, frequency, visits authorized, visits used, visits already booked, and the date the plan must be recertified.
: each appointment with the billed units, copay collected and whether the note is signed.

Enter every active patient's plan of care with authorized visits and the recertification date. Copy the dates from the signed plan, not from memory.

Imani's knee plan allows 24 visits. She has completed 15 and has 6 booked. Visits left to book shows 3, and the Authorization column is still OK. When she completes 21, it changes to Request more visits, which is the moment to send a progress note and ask the payer for more.
